title: Plumage diversity without differential expression of pigmentation genes in a rapid avian radiation
abstract: Uncovering the molecular basis of reproductive traits is key to understanding species divergence. Capuchino Seedeaters (  Sporophila ), a radiation of genetically similar birds differing mainly in male reproductive plumage color, can be leveraged to study how such traits evolve. Outlier scans identified candidate pigmentation variants primarily in noncoding sequence, implying regulatory changes. However, RNA-seq of growing feather follicles generally did not show differential expression of pigmentation genes among different colors, with only  ASIP downregulated in crown feathers. Gene expression patterns instead varied by body region. The largest difference between dimorphic sexes was the upregulation of the carotenoid-degrading gene  BCO2 in males, accompanied by lower carotenoid content in male feathers. An improved genome annotation assigned 9.5% of candidate variants into coding and untranslated sequence. This suggests species-diagnostic variants lie within transcribed sequence and could act post-transcriptionally, rather than through transcript abundance, leading to a revised hypothesis for plumage divergence in this radiation.
authors: Recuerda M, Repenning M, Toomey MB, Kraemer S, Rosoni JRR, Silveira LF, Kopuchian C, Campagna L.

title: Multiomics Analysis of Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma Reveals the Immunological Microenvironment Associated with MTAP Loss and Immunotherapy Outcomes.
abstract: PurposeNivolumab plus ipilimumab is a standard first-line therapy for unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), yet biomarkers predicting immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy remain undefined. We aimed to identify genomic and tumor immune microenvironmental features associated with ICI response in MPM.Experimental designWe analyzed two independent MPM cohorts. The discovery cohort included patients at the National Cancer Center Hospital (2012-2022) with frozen tumor tissues available for whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and RNA sequencing. Genomic alterations, transcriptomic profiles, immune cell composition, and T-cell receptor repertoire were analyzed, and key findings were validated in a nationwide Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics (C-CAT) cohort.ResultsThe WGS cohort comprised 52 patients. Among ICI-treated patients, overall response rates were 30% in the WGS cohort and 29.4% in the C-CAT cohort. Genomic analyses identified frequent alterations in BAP1 and NF2, across both cohorts. ICI responders showed higher T-cell receptor diversity, increased CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and enrichment of M1 macrophages compared with non-responders. MTAP loss was associated with higher CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and T-cell receptor diversity, and was linked to a higher ICI response rate in the C-CAT cohort. In contrast, BAP1 and NF2 alterations showed no consistent association with immune features or ICI efficacy.ConclusionsAn immune-active tumor microenvironment characterized by high T-cell receptor diversity, CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and M1 macrophage enrichment was associated with favorable ICI responses in MPM. MTAP loss was linked to immune-related features and a higher ICI response, supporting further investigation of MTAP loss as a candidate biomarker.
journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
authors: Tateishi A, Yoshida T, Shiraishi K, Uehara Y, Gosho K, Miyakoshi J, Torasawa M, Igawa YS, Kitadai R, Yoshida Y, Shinno Y, Matsumoto Y, Okuma Y, Mizutani T, Horinouchi H, Koyama T, Watanabe SI, Yatabe Y, Yamamoto N, Kohno T, Goto Y.

title: Pseudomonas sediminis CRE-TB-54 carries tmexCD3-toprJ3 in a novel chromosomal region.
abstract: The emergence of tmexCD-toprJ, coding for a transmissible multidrug resistance efflux pump of the resistance-nodulation-division (RND) family has compromised the usefulness of tigecycline in the treatment of infections caused by multidrug resistant Gram-negative bacteria. Here, we describe the presence of tmexCD3-toprJ3 in a novel chromosomal context in Pseudomonas sediminis CRE-TB-54 isolated from a toilet in a university dormitory in southwestern Nigeria. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole genome sequencing showed that CRE-TB-54 displayed intermediate level resistance to tigecycline and haboured multiple antibiotic resistance genes, including tmexCD3-toprJ3 flanked upstream and downstream by genetic structures not previously reported in association with tmexCD-toprJ. These include insertion sequences IS4 and IS30, and the metal resistance gene czcD upstream, the prophage integrase IntA, the competence associated DNA binding protein gene comEA, and the double stranded DNA repair and homologous recombination gene cluster recBCD downstream. These results provide new insight into the genetic structures surrounding the tmexCD-toprJ cluster and raises concern about toilets as a potential environmental reservoir of bacteria carrying this clinically important gene in a resource-limited setting where tigecycline is not currently used in human or animals.
authors: Olufemi Adelowo O, Fashae K, Babajide Taiwo J, Kaster AK, Müller JA.

title: Advances and challenges in tissue-based HIV reservoir quantification.
abstract: Purpose of reviewPeripheral blood provides an accessible but incomplete representation of the HIV reservoir. This review summarizes recent advances in PCR-based quantification of HIV persistence in human tissues, with particular emphasis on the intact proviral DNA assay (IPDA), the methodological challenges introduced by tissue sampling, and complementary approaches that extend the biological information obtained from IPDA.Recent findingsIPDA and related droplet digital PCR assays are increasingly being applied to human tissues, including lymph nodes, brain, gut, and adipose tissue, often in combination with orthogonal assays to address specific biological questions. Recent studies highlight important considerations in interpreting these measurements, particularly the identity and number of cells used as the denominator, DNA shearing, and spatial representativeness of the sampled tissue. These issues complicate comparisons across tissues and with peripheral blood, particularly when different cell populations or sampling depths are analyzed. Newer multitarget droplet digital PCR assays increase the genomic information used to infer proviral intactness, while complementary approaches provide information on viral genotype, cellular identity, clonality, and functional state.SummaryRecent applications of IPDA to human tissues highlight important considerations in cellular denominator, sampling depth, DNA shearing, and spatial sampling that influence the interpretation of reservoir measurements across anatomical compartments. At the same time, combining IPDA with complementary assays is extending tissue studies beyond quantification toward characterization of the virus, infected cell, clonality, and functional state. Future approaches that preserve the relationship between the virus, its host cell, and its tissue environment will further advance the study of HIV persistence in tissues.
journal: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
authors: Lee GQ, Simonetti FR.

title: Molecular detection of Coxiella burnetii and a Coxiellaceae bacterium in Hyalomma asiaticum and Dermacentor nuttalli ticks collected in Mongolia.
abstract: Coxiella burnetii, the causative agent of Q fever, is a zoonotic pathogen for which epidemiological data are limited in Mongolia. This study investigated the presence of C. burnetii in ticks collected across Mongolia from forest, pasture, and livestock-associated environments. A total of 7,511 ticks were collected from 42 Soums across 12 provinces and 2 districts of Ulaanbaatar between May and June 2018. Molecular detection of Coxiella-related organisms was performed using 46 DNA samples, comprising 28 individual-tick samples and 18 pooled-tick samples representing 489 ticks, by nested PCR targeting IS1111 and the 16S rRNA gene. Twenty DNA samples (2 individual ticks and 18 pools) were PCR-positive. Sequencing and phylogenetic analysis revealed that 9 Hyalomma asiaticum tick pools contained 16S rRNA sequences of C. burnetii, whereas 11 Dermacentor nuttalli samples (2 individual ticks and 9 pools) contained 16S rRNA sequences of a Coxiellaceae bacterium. Two individual D. nuttalli ticks yielded IS1111 sequences closely related to C. burnetii, whereas the corresponding 16S rRNA sequences clustered with a Coxiellaceae bacterium, highlighting discordance between the 2 molecular targets. The C. burnetii sequences detected in H. asiaticum were closely related to clade A strains reported from the United States, Japan, Greenland, and Korea, whereas sequences detected in D. nuttalli clustered with Coxiella endosymbiont sequences. This study provides molecular evidence for the presence of C. burnetii in H. asiaticum tick pools in Mongolia and demonstrates that Mongolian ticks harbor genetically diverse Coxiella-related bacteria, highlighting the need for further investigation of their epidemiological significance.
authors: Kim CM, Kh T, Lp MJ, Lee YM, D G, B N, J B, N T, Yun NR, Kim DM.

title: Genomic analysis of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with a severe episode of self-trauma and urinary tract infection.
abstract: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales are emerging pathogens of major importance in veterinary medicine. This study describes the clinical, microbiological, and genomic characteristics of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with paraparesis and concurrent pyelonephritis, chronic cystitis, and a self-traumatized limb lesion. A 12-year-old mixed-breed female dog underwent repeated antimicrobial therapy during hospitalization. Urine obtained by cystocentesis and wound samples were cultured, and ESBL-producing strains were characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequence-based analysis. CTX-M-55-producing E. coli sequence type (ST) 457, phylogroup F, O11:H25, and fimH145, was recovered from urine and wound samples, while the wound sample also yielded a CTX-M-15- and SHV-2-producing K. pneumoniae ST39, KL149:OL2α.2. The two closely related E. coli strains differed by 96 single nucleotide polymorphisms, despite sharing the same ST, resistome, plasmid replicons, and virulence profile. ESBL-positive strains carried multiple virulence genes, with the E. coli strains classified as extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli strains. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae ST39 in an animal in Brazil. The co-occurrence of ESBL-producing E. coli ST457 and K. pneumoniae ST39 in the same dog highlights the potential for companion animals to harbor clinically relevant multidrug-resistant lineages and reinforces the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship in this sector.
authors: Repossi CP, Paiva SC, Simões MN, Fernandes BM, Silva JVO, de Araújo TA, Ferraz CM, Senhorello ILS, Rossi GAM, Furlan JPR.

title: Comprehensive meta-QTL analysis uncovers stable loci for fruit traits, morphological development, anthocyanin regulation, and biotic stress resistance in eggplant.
abstract: Eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) is a crop of significant nutritional value within the Solanaceae family; however, advancements in breeding for fruit quality, stress resilience, and architectural traits are limited due to the quantitative nature of inheritance for these traits. Meta-QTL (MQTL) analysis provides a powerful approach for integrating QTL information from various studies for identifying stable genomic regions. We integrated 620 initial QTLs derived from 23 independent studies that encompass traits related to morphology, fruit characteristics, anthocyanin content, prickles, and resistance to biotic stress. A high-density consensus genetic framework was constructed, onto which 425 QTLs (68.54%) were successfully projected. Meta-analysis identified 97 stable MQTLs across LG1-LG12, with the mean confidence interval decreasing from 10.29 cM for the initial QTLs to 3.42 cM for the MQTLs, corresponding to an approximately threefold reduction in interval width (66.8% narrowing). Candidate gene mining within 40 prioritized MQTLs resulted in the retrieval of 1,440 gene models, which were subsequently refined to 68 high-confidence candidates. This refinement was based on domain architecture, synteny conservation with tomato and potato, ortholog analysis, and expression profiling. Key genomic hubs were identified across several chromosomes, most notably on Chromosome 6, which acts as a multi-trait super-region housing major loci for anthocyanin pigmentation (MQTL6.4_A), morphological traits (MQTL6.3_M), and prickle development (MQTL6.3_P). Other critical intervals include Chromosome 3 (MQTL3.1_Bs) for biotic stress resistance, and Chromosomes 1 and 4 (MQTL1.1_F, MQTL4.3_F) for fruit quality traits. These hotspots are enriched for coordinated, multi-layered regulatory networks and functional modules, including pattern-recognition receptors (e.g., LRR-RLKs), transcriptional regulators (WRKY, MYB), scaffolding proteins, and specialized metabolic and structural enzymes (such as GDSL esterases, laccases, F-box proteins, and SWEET transporters). The significant conservation of synteny with both tomato and potato, along with functional insights from Arabidopsis orthology, underscores the evolutionary stability and functional importance of these co-adapted candidate gene complexes across the Solanaceae. This study represents the first comprehensive MQTL analysis in eggplant, establishing a robust genomic framework for trait improvement, providing key markers and candidate genes to accelerate marker-assisted selection and genomic breeding aimed at developing climate-resilient, high-quality varieties.
journal: TAG. Theoretical and applied genetics. Theoretische und angewandte Genetik
authors: Hossain MY, Ahmed M, Islam MR, Rana MS, Ananty NT, Turzo MTA, Hasan J, Khan IMM, Banu MSA, Hossin AY, Huda KMK, Parveen S, Rashid MH.

title: Genetic disruptions of Hsp90-encoding genes impacted short-term evolutionary trajectories of antifungal resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
abstract: Laboratory evolution has been a powerful approach to address questions about evolvability. It has been debated whether the molecular chaperone heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) buffers or potentiates the effects of variation and, consequently, constrains or accelerates evolution. In this study, we experimentally evolved yeast strains carrying mutant alleles of Hsp90-encoding genes under mild clotrimazole selection. We found that knockout of HSC82, which encodes a constitutively expressed Hsp90 chaperone, led to slower evolution of clotrimazole resistance in the short term. However, all strains generally evolved resistance within seven transfers, regardless of Hsp90 status. Through whole-genome sequencing, we identified genetic changes associated with clotrimazole resistance, including prevalent mitochondrial genome loss, as well as chromosomal duplications and point mutations. HSC82 knockout populations specifically showed convergent chromosomal duplications of chrVIII and chrXV. Taken together, our results demonstrate that disruption of Hsp90 in yeast may not alter the overall outcome of evolution but may shape its evolutionary trajectories at both the phenotypic and genotypic levels.
authors: Li XC, Liang M, Han X, Li W, Dou F.

title: Genital microbial profile of repeat breeding in a Kangal sheep flock: a survey of ewes and rams under natural mating.
abstract: Infertility in sheep remains a significant concern in modern livestock production, with non-pregnancy rates during the breeding season increasing considerably in recent decades. The present study was conducted in a Kangal sheep flock with a documented history of reproductive failure, characterised by consecutive estrous cycles without conception. A total of 905 multiparous Kangal ewes (3-6 years old) and 44 Kangal rams (4-6 years old), all with documented fertility records, were enrolled at the beginning of the breeding season. Before mating, all ewes underwent transrectal ultrasonographic examination and evaluation of vaginal discharge. Following this screening, 880 ewes with no ultrasonographic abnormalities and normal vaginal discharge were monitored throughout the breeding season. Of these, 171 ewes that failed to conceive after the first mating underwent a second mating cycle, resulting in 50 additional pregnancies. The remaining 121 non-pregnant ewes underwent a third mating, resulting in 36 additional pregnancies. Blood samples were subsequently collected from the 85 ewes that remained non-pregnant after three consecutive mating attempts. Of these, 21 tested seropositive for Coxiella burnetii and border disease virus (BDV) and were excluded from the study. Vaginal swabs were collected from 25 of the remaining 64 ewes that tested negative for Brucella spp., C. burnetii, and BDV. These animals were classified as repeat breeders or clinically affected animals (Group 2). An equal number of ewes ( n=25 ) that tested negative for these pathogens and conceived after a single mating cycle were assigned to the healthy control group (Group 1). Preputial swabs were also collected from 15 breeding rams to evaluate the potential for venereal transmission. All swab samples were subjected to microbiological culture and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis following DNA extraction. The targeted pathogens included Brucella spp., Mycoplasma spp., Chlamydophila spp., Campylobacter spp., Coxiella burnetii, Salmonella Abortusovis, Trueperella pyogenes, and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Although Mycoplasma spp., T. pyogenes, and Campylobacter spp. were detected in swab samples from both groups, the prevalence of Mycoplasma spp. ( padjMycoplasma bovigenitalium ( padj=0.05 ) was significantly higher in Group 2 than in Group 1. The increased detection of these microorganisms in reproductively compromised ewes suggests a potential role in the aetiology of ovine infertility, either through direct pathogenic effects or by contributing to reproductive tract dysbiosis. However, further controlled studies are warranted to establish a definitive causal relationship between these microorganisms and reproductive failure in sheep.
authors: Takcı A, Moğulkoç MN, Kıvrak MB, Kalın R, Demirel MA, Sönmez Ünal G.

title: Climate-Associated Genetic Variation in Native and Introduced Populations of Eustenopus villosus, a Biological Control Agent for Yellow Starthistle.
abstract: Contemporary evolution in biological control systems is rarely studied, though biological agents are repeatedly exposed to novel environmental conditions upon introduction. Their ability to adapt to new conditions could influence management efficacy and reveal important aspects of environmental selection. Using a ddRADseq dataset, we tested for genomic evidence of adaptation to climate in populations of Eustenopus villosus (Boheman, Coleoptera: Curculionidae), the "hairy weevil", which is used in classical biological control for yellow starthistle (Centaurea solstitialis L., Asteraceae) in the western United States. We first estimated population structure in E. villosus across our samples of the native and introduced ranges and then used six complementary genotype-environment association analyses to identify single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with climate in both native and introduced populations. Additionally, we used historical release records to categorize sampling sites according to their serial founding history and test for impacts of this history on total and putatively adaptive genomic variation in the introductions. We also tested whether candidate loci associated with climate in the native range exhibit similar associations in the introductions, or if new associations have evolved. We identified many candidate loci in both native and introduced populations and found little evidence of a decline in genomic variation, which suggests that serial founding events did not prevent climatic adaptation. Candidate loci differed between native and introduced populations, indicating that local adaptation has occurred in different regions of the genome after introduction of E. villosus. Our findings suggest an important role for novel contemporary adaptation in this biological control system and provide insight into how genetic variation can persist in biological control agents through introduction and serial founding events.
authors: Barker BS, Pelosi JA, Sert O, Dlugosch KM.

title: Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.
abstract: Cognitive impairment in cirrhosis is associated with an altered gut‒liver‒brain axis, but geographic variations in diet and clinical practices may limit generalizability. We investigated consistency of microbial signatures for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment across four countries. We enrolled outpatients with cirrhosis from USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico who underwent Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE), and stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic and functional associations with PHES were evaluated after adjustment for MELD, country, demographics, sex, proton pump inhibitor (PPI), lactulose, and rifaximin use. We enrolled 221 patients (median age 58 y, 57.9% men, median MELD 12). Cognitive performance varied by country despite adjustment for clinical covariates. Lithuania demonstrated greater microbial richness and better cognition despite higher MELD, accompanied by distinct dietary patterns including greater yogurt and tea consumption. In the entire cohort, increasing MELD was associated with reduced microbial richness and depletion of commensals. Worse PHES performance, however, showed a distinct microbiome signature with increased Streptococcus abundance independent of MELD, country, PPI use, and HE therapies. Twenty-two microbial pathways were associated with PHES, mostly related to amino-acid biosynthesis and nitrogen metabolism. Of these, ornithine degradation and heme B biosynthesis II were uniquely enriched with worse PHES and CHE, which mapped onto Enterobacteriaceae. We conclude that across four geographically and culturally disparate countries, cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment was associated with consistent microbial compositional and functional alterations distinct from advancing liver disease. These findings support a consistent gut‒liver‒brain axis signature involving oral-gut translocation and altered nitrogen metabolism.
authors: Sommer AJ, Kiudeliene E, Lauridsen M, Torre A, Fagan A, Skieceviciene J, Jonasson E, Obolewicz H, Sikaroodi M, Kupcinskas J, Khoruts A, Gillevet PM, Bajaj JS.

title: Microbial mechanisms of enhancing carbon and nitrogen conversion by segmented sodium acetate dosing in a modified A<sup>2</sup>/O process.
abstract: Low C/N ratios in municipal wastewater often limit nitrogen removal efficiency, necessitating carbon source supplementation to enhance denitrification and reduce effluent total nitrogen (TN) concentrations. This study addresses this challenge by establishing a feast-famine alternating nutritional environment in a modified anaerobic-anoxic-oxic (MAAO) reactor through segmented sodium acetate dosing. This approach was associated with enhanced carbon and nitrogen metabolic pathway conversions. Our results showed that segmented sodium acetate dosing was associated with improved microbial substrate uptake, leading to increased carbon and nitrogen conversion rates of 2.3 percentage points and 11.8 percentage points, respectively. Enhanced interactions between hydrolyzing/fermenting bacteria and denitrifying bacteria fostered synergistic carbon and nitrogen conversion. Furthermore, metagenomic analysis indicated enhanced genetic potential for nitrate transport and denitrification, consistent with the increased denitrification contribution observed in the nitrogen balance. This research illuminates the efficiency of carbon and nitrogen metabolism and microbial community function in MAAO in response to dynamic nutrient environments. It contributes significantly to understanding the potential mechanisms underlying nitrogen transformation in such systems.
authors: Wang S, Li W, Zhang G, Guo X, Li D, Yao S, Fang R, Liu P, Huang K.

title: Combination antiviral treatment for a patient with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus meningoencephalitis associated with bispecific antibody teclistamab therapy for myeloma.
abstract: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) is a rare cause of meningoencephalitis in humans. Although LCMV is a rodent zoonosis with a global distribution, no UK cases in humans have been reported in published literature since the 1950s, and testing is rarely performed. LCMV meningoencephalitis is self-limiting in people who are immunocompetent, but infection in hosts who are immunocompromised causes severe disease. We report a presentation of LCMV meningoencephalitis in a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma receiving teclistamab. The patient presented with a 5-month history of progressive neurological symptoms, including hearing loss, ataxia, headache, and weight loss. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed lymphocytic pleocytosis, markedly elevated protein concentration, and hypoglycorrhachia. Extensive microbiological and autoimmune investigations were negative, and empirical antimicrobial and antituberculosis therapies did not prevent clinical deterioration. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of CSF identified LCMV, and a history of domestic rodent exposure was subsequently identified. Combination antiviral therapy with ribavirin, remdesivir, and molnupiravir was initiated. Molnupiravir was later substituted for favipiravir, and favipiravir dosing was guided by serum and CSF therapeutic drug monitoring. The patient showed sustained neurological improvement, with clearance of LCMV from CSF and blood within 2 months. Antiviral therapy continued for 6 months. The patient regained functional independence and returned to work, with only mild residual symptoms. In addition to reporting a novel occurrence of LCMV infection in a patient on teclistamab, the case highlights the presence of LCMV in the UK and the utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for pathogen identification in undiagnosed encephalitis. Finally, the case provides preliminary evidence supporting combination antiviral therapy in persistent LCMV infection.

title: Harnessing phage defense systems to develop a Burkholderia bacterial host.
abstract: Heterologous production of metabolites and proteins requires the transfer of foreign DNA into a host. One common barrier to the genetic engineering of bacteria is their plethora of phage defense systems. Targeted deletion of defense system components can improve DNA transfer for downstream applications. We sought to improve the transformation efficiency of Burkholderia sp. FERM BP-3421, a β-proteobacterial host that has great potential for the high-titer production of bioactive small molecules. We investigated restriction-modification systems and the recently described Kiwa phage defense system. Through deletion of three restriction enzyme genes, transformation efficiency was improved nearly 7-fold. The electroporation protocol was also optimized with respect to temperature, cell density, and buffer composition, which resulted in an additional 40-fold improvement in transformation efficiency, reaching 1 × 106 CFU/µg plasmid DNA. Interestingly, a mimicry by methylation approach, where DNA is pre-methylated using two host DNA methyltransferases, outperformed the transformation efficiency obtained with restriction enzyme deletion mutants nearly 3-fold. Moreover, contrary to previous reports in Escherichia coli, deletion of the Kiwa system did not improve transformation efficiency into Burkholderia sp. FERM BP-3421. Understanding the impact of bacterial innate immune systems on genetic tractability is vital to improving non-model host strains to produce high-value molecules of interest.ImportanceThe ability to transfer DNA into bacteria is key to genetic engineering. However, bacteria have evolved immune defenses to recognize and protect themselves from foreign DNA, thwarting genetic manipulation. Here, we identified putative defense systems in a β-proteobacterial strain of interest and characterized their impact on DNA transfer. The defense systems studied belong to the well-known class of restriction-modification systems and to the recently described Kiwa system. Intriguingly, we observed higher DNA transfer efficiency by avoiding restriction-modification systems via pre-methylation rather than by restriction gene deletion. Future studies should investigate the underlying mechanism for this difference. Moreover, contrary to what was reported for γ-proteobacteria Escherichia coli, we showed that the Kiwa system does not impair DNA transfer into the β-proteobacteria Burkholderia sp. strain. There has been significant interest in the discovery of novel defense systems. Learning more about their complexity is important to enable genetic manipulation of previously intractable strains.
authors: Heard SC, Ptacek GM, Kadjo AE, Eustáquio AS.

title: An integrated cell culture-nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq) method for the simultaneous detection of multiple enterovirus types and quantification of infectious Enterovirus B.
abstract: Enteroviruses (EVs) are ubiquitous contaminants of surface waters, where they can remain infectious for long periods of time. Most methods used for EV monitoring are unable to distinguish between infectious and non-infectious particles, or between EV types. Because different types exhibit both distinct environmental persistence and health implications, there is a need for type-resolved infectivity measurements. Here, we developed integrated cell culture-nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq), a method combining short-term cell culture amplification with nanopore sequencing of the VP1 gene. The ICC approach was adapted from a previously described ICC-reverse transcriptase quantitative PCR (ICC-RTqPCR) protocol, while the NanoporeSeq workflow was derived from a clinical EV typing protocol and optimized for environmentally circulating EV types. Using samples containing known concentrations of 10 EV types, the NanoporeSeq method accurately and reproducibly recovered the original proportions of all EV types after correction of biases. When applied to wastewater extracts, the method detected 45 EV types across five species. Furthermore, type-specific calibration curves generated with ICC-NanoporeSeq enabled quantification of the infectious concentrations of six EV types of the Enterovirus B species, allowing a simultaneous and type-resolved assessment of infectivity in mixed samples. Overall, ICC-NanoporeSeq provides a scalable approach for the parallel analysis of multiple EV types. Compared with the predecessor ICC-RTqPCR method, it eliminates the need for multiple type-specific PCR primers, and can therefore be readily expanded to include additional EV types.IMPORTANCECurrent methods used to detect enteroviruses (EVs) in environmental samples generally measure viral genome copies without determining whether viruses remain infectious, limiting their use in public health risk assessment or water quality monitoring. At the same time, available infectivity assays are often labor-intensive and cannot distinguish between different EV types. Here, we developed integrated cell culture-nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq), a method combining cell culture and nanopore sequencing to simultaneously quantify the infectious concentrations of multiple EV types in samples containing mixed EV populations. The method provides an efficient and scalable approach for studying EVs in complex environmental matrices. ICC-NanoporeSeq has potential applications in wastewater-based epidemiology, environmental surveillance, and disinfection studies, where understanding the persistence of different EV types simultaneously is crucial.
authors: Astorch-Cardona A, Rouault S, Kohn T.

title: PCR-amplified blaKPC-2-triggered Cas12a activation coupled with DNA cube-confined Fc reporter cleavage on a Ti<sub>3</sub>C<sub>2</sub>/CsPbBr<sub>3</sub>@PDA@Au/GCE dual-mode ECL/SERS interface.
abstract: Rapid and reliable detection of antibiotic resistance genes is essential for guiding antimicrobial therapy and controlling the spread of carbapenem-resistant pathogens. Herein, we developed a PCR amplicon-activated CRISPR/Cas12a-regulated dual-mode electrochemiluminescence/surface-enhanced Raman scattering biosensor for sensitive detection of the blaKPC-2 resistance gene. A specific blaKPC-2 fragment containing the selected TTTG PAM region was amplified by PCR and used as a double-stranded DNA activator for the crRNA/Cas12a complex. After target recognition, activated Cas12a cleaved the Fc-labeled reporter segments integrated into a DNA cube scaffold assembled on the Ti3C2/CsPbBr3@PDA@Au nanocomposite interface. In the initial state, Fc was positioned close to the Ti3C2/CsPbBr3@PDA@Au-modified GCE surface, resulting in ECL quenching and strong SERS emission. Upon Cas12a-mediated cleavage of the exposed ssDNA reporter segments, Fc-containing fragments were released from the interface, leading to ECL recovery and SERS attenuation. Therefore, the target-induced process enabled an anti-correlated ECL-on/SERS-off signal conversion, and the ratiometric value R = IECL/ISERS was used for quantitative analysis. The concentration-dependent response was empirically fitted over 10-107 copies per µL, whereas the 108 copies per µL group exhibited upper-range response compression. Boundary back-calculation indicated that further quantitative validation is required. Blank-response inverse prediction gave a model-dependent response-equivalent concentration of approximately 1.06 copies per µL; Poisson sampling gave a 95% molecular-sampling threshold of approximately 3.0 copies per µL for a 1.0 µL input. Neither descriptor is an experimentally determined detection or quantification limit. The platform also exhibited good selectivity against other resistance genes and non-target bacterial genomic DNA, together with satisfactory repeatability, reproducibility, stability, and acceptable spike-recovery performance in 10% diluted serum as a model biological matrix, providing preliminary evidence of matrix tolerance rather than clinical validation. This work provides a self-calibrated dual-mode strategy for antibiotic resistance gene detection, while further validation using bacterial lysates, extracted bacterial genomic DNA, and clinical bacterial isolates is required before diagnostic application. qPCR supported linear amplification over 10-107 copies per µL; endpoint responses remained observable through 108 copies per µL, where quantitative resolution was reduced.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
authors: Chen Y, Huang J, Wen L, Zhu Q, Liu J, Meng J, Yu L.

title: Antibacterial and Virulence-Modulating Activities of Bacillus velezensis JM3 Against Pectobacterium carotovorum subsp. carotovorum PCC21.
abstract: Bacterial soft-rot caused by Pectobacterium carotovorum subsp. carotovorum (Pcc) is associated with quorum sensing (QS), motility, and plant cell wall degrading enzymes. In this study, strain JM3, isolated from the rhizosphere of Chinese cabbage, was identified as Bacillus velezensis based on gyrB, 16S rRNA and rpoB phylogenetic analyses. JM3 showed strong antibacterial activity against Pcc strain PCC21 and significantly reduced soft-rot lesions in Chinese cabbage leaf sections. An ethyl acetate extract of the JM3 cell-free supernatant (CFS) showed concentration-dependent antibacterial activity, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 1 mg/mL. The acid-treated cell-free supernatant (AT-CFS), following acid treatment of the JM3 CFS and removal of the resulting precipitate, showed markedly reduced antibacterial activity, with an MIC of 8 mg/mL. At 0.5 mg/mL (1/16 MIC), AT-CFS did not markedly affect PCC21 growth but reduced N-acyl homoserine lactone associated signals, swarming motility, and extracellular protease, pectate lyase, and cellulase activities. RT-qPCR analysis revealed reduced expression of QS-related genes (expI and expR), extracellular enzyme genes (pelB, pehA, celA, and prt1), and motilityassociated genes (motA and flhC). These findings suggest that JM3 antagonizes PCC21 through both direct growth inhibition and extracellular activities affecting QS and virulence-associated traits under growth-noninhibitory conditions. The results provide a basis for further characterization of JM3 derived extracellular metabolites involved in interactions with the soft-rot pathogen.
authors: Lee D, Seo H, Kang M, Jeong T, Seo G, Jung Y, Seo YS.

title: Diagnostic Value in Discarded Reads: Re-evaluating Multi-Mapping cfDNA Fragmentomics and GC Bias in Early-Stage Cancer.
abstract: Background:  Low-coverage plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing is an inexpensive substrate for cancer detection. Standard pipelines discard fragments with low mapping quality, which originate mostly from repetitive DNA, although pericentromeric satellite repeats are frequently hypomethylated in cancer. We asked whether the fraction of multi-mapping cfDNA fragments differs between early-stage cancer and matched healthy controls, and how it compares with conventional fragmentomic features under strict control of technical factors. Methods. We analysed public plasma cfDNA whole-genome sequencing from 25 patients with stage I to III breast cancer and 25 healthy controls matched 1:1 for age, sex, smoking and alcohol use, each pair processed in the same library and sequencing batch, and from 8 early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases with 8 matched controls. For every sample we computed the fraction of autosomal fragments with MAPQ < 30 and the share of these fragments located in centromeric and heterochromatic cytobands, and related them to stage, grade and copy-number deviation as proxies of tumour burden. Classifiers were evaluated by leave-one-pair-out cross-validation in breast cancer and, trained on breast cancer only, applied unchanged to HCC. Robustness to GC content and sequencing depth was tested by within-fold residualisation and by fragment-level GC weighting. Conventional fragmentomic features (fragment length, end motifs, copy number, DELFI-like profiles and window features at transcription start sites) were evaluated under four GC-handling analyses. Results. The multi-mapping fraction was higher in breast cancer than in matched controls (median 5.38 % vs 5.19 %; higher in 19/25 pairs; paired p = 0.0006; cross-validated AUC 0.81, 95 % CI 0.67 - 0.94), in stage I (9/10 pairs), stage II (7/10) and stage III (3/5) disease and in every sequencing batch. The excess was concentrated in centromeric and heterochromatic bands, whose share of multi-mapping fragments rose from 22.0 % to 23.4 % (19/25 pairs; p = 0.004). Both signals persisted after within-fold adjustment for GC content and/or depth (AUC 0.64 - 0.76 for the multi-mapping fraction, 0.71 - 0.76 for the heterochromatic share) and under fragment-level GC weighting (18/25 pairs; p = 0.003). The multi-mapping difference was largest in stage I and decreased with stage (Spearman ρ = −0.42, p = 0.04), and neither feature was associated with grade or copy-number deviation. In public tissue methylomes, satellites were hypomethylated in breast tumours to a similar extent as other late-replicating DNA, but the bin-level association between tumour hypomethylation and the cfDNA excess was weak and was explained by GC content. In HCC, the pre-specified endpoint, the breast-trained multi-mapping model, was not met (AUC 0.73; 5/8 pairs; sign test p = 0.36). In an exploratory analysis that was not pre-specified, the heterochromatic share was higher in 7/8 HCC pairs (p = 0.016; locked AUC 0.86, 95 % CI 0.62 - 1.00); across all 33 pairs, including the discovery pairs, it was higher in the cancer case in 26 (post hoc sign test p = 0.0007). In contrast, conventional fragmentomic features reached AUC 0.71 (breast) and 0.77 (HCC) only without fragment-level GC control; they tracked the per-sample coverage GC dependence and fell to chance under each of three GC-controlled analyses, including one that preserves promoter-specific signal. Conclusions. Multi-mapping cfDNA fragments, which are routinely discarded, differed between early-stage breast cancer and batch-matched controls, largely independently of GC content and sequencing depth, with an excess in centromeric and heterochromatic DNA. The signal did not scale with stage, its biological origin is unproven, and a read-quality contribution cannot be excluded from fragment files. It is a candidate marker that requires confirmation in larger cohorts with raw reads and tumour-fraction estimates.
authors: UPPALURI KR, Challa HJ, Vempati KK, Kadali LN.

title: Analysing antimicrobial resistance mobility patterns using a diverse dataset of over 8000 bacterial species
abstract: Advances in genomics have enhanced surveillance of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the factors governing resistance gene mobility, and therefore their risk of spread, remain poorly characterized. Here, we analyzed AMR gene distributions across thousands of bacterial genomes from NCBI RefSeq, encompassing clinical, agricultural and environmental isolates, to quantify associations with plasmids and predicted mobile genomic islands. AMR genes were identified using the Resistance Gene Identifier, and in addition to plasmid identification, mobile chromosomal elements were predicted using IslandViewer 4. Analysing both the full dataset and subsets of data with corrections for sampling bias, we show that known AMR genes are significantly enriched in mobile regions overall. However, stratification by resistance mechanism supported marked heterogeneity: certain drug classes and mechanisms are strongly associated with mobile elements, whereas others are predominantly chromosomal and non-mobile. Notably, mechanisms with specialized functions showed higher mobility, consistent with their role as “ecological public goods” that need not be present in all cells to confer community-level benefit. Differences were also observed across bacteria with distinct cell envelope structures. Together, these findings lay the groundwork for predictive models of AMR gene mobility and provide a framework for incorporating gene-level mobility into AMR risk assessment and antimicrobial stewardship policy.
authors: Jia B, Alcock BP, Raphenya AR, Spence J, Maguire F, Beiko RG, McArthur AG, Bertelli C, Brinkman FS.

title: Genomic Regions Associated with Resistance to Soybean Cyst Nematode (Heterodera glycines) Population HG Type 1.2.5.7 in Dry Beans (Phaseolus vulgaris).
abstract: North Dakota, the largest dry bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) producing state in the United States, faces an emerging production threat caused by the soybean cyst nematode (SCN; Heterodera glycines Ichinohe, 1952). Host resistance is an effective management strategy, yet resistance to the virulent SCN population HG type 1.2.5.7 has not been genetically characterized in dry beans. In this study, 170 dry bean genotypes (113 breeding lines/cultivars and 57 germplasm accessions) were evaluated for response to HG type 1.2.5.7 under controlled conditions using the female index (FI) as the resistance phenotype. FI values ranged from 4.1 to 78.1%, with one genotype (PI 313733) classified as resistant, 35 moderately resistant, 104 moderately susceptible, and 30 susceptible. Genome-wide association analysis using 2,044 single-nucleotide polymorphism markers from the 3.8K Bean Panel chip and the BLINK model identified four significant marker-trait associations on chromosomes Pv02, Pv05, Pv07, and Pv11. Linkage disequilibrium-defined candidate intervals spanned 108 kb (Pv02), 1.50 Mb (Pv05), 798 kb (Pv07), and 1.45 Mb (Pv11), collectively containing 126 annotated genes: 20 on Pv02, 39 on Pv05, 35 on Pv07, and 32 on Pv11. The intervals contained putative genes annotated for signaling and transcriptional regulation, cell wall and carbohydrate metabolism, transport, and secondary metabolism. Together, these findings indicate that the response to HG type 1.2.5.7 in dry bean is quantitative and associated with multiple genomic regions. The identified intervals provide candidate targets for independent validation, fine mapping, functional analysis, and future marker development to support breeding for SCN resistance.
authors: Poudyal P, Figueroa-Cerna J, Osorno JM, Singh G, Yan G.

title: From smartphone to gene: Automated image-based phenotyping captures flowering diversity of common buckwheat
abstract: Common buckwheat (  Fagopyrum esculentum Moench) exhibits an indeterminate flowering habit, resulting in the simultaneous occurrence of flowering, seed development and seed ripening. This contributes to yield losses and complicates mechanized harvesting. Therefore, the development of varieties with a desirable flowering pattern is a breeding priority in buckwheat. However, phenotyping of buckwheat flowering under field conditions remains challenging because manual assessments are time consuming and expertise dependent. Here, we show that imaging devices such as smartphones or cameras can be used for phenotyping of flowering traits in a buckwheat collection encompassing 169 accessions. Flowering traits describing flowering time (  n =10), flowering intensity (  n =6) and abscission (  n =6) were extracted from 37,078 images captured over five growing seasons using a Mask R-CNN segmentation model combined with statistical modelling of flowering dynamics. The 22 extracted traits were highly heritable (0.5 < ℎ  2 < 0.93) and correlated well (0.84 <  r < 0.94) with manually assessed flowering stages while providing additional information on flowering intensity. Genome-wide association studies revealed 171 genomic regions associated with flowering traits, including marker-trait associations for agronomically important breeding targets. Candidate genes had functional annotations including “Auxin response factor” and “Ethylene-insensitive protein”, gene families involved in hormone signalling and developmental regulation, controlling flowering in other species. These results demonstrate how digital imaging combined with automated feature extraction can be leveraged to gain insight on buckwheat flowering patterns in large scale field trials across different phenotyping platforms. This paves the way to breed for desired flowering patterns using molecular tools in a targeted manner.
authors: Quesada-Traver C, Hess F, Tschurr F, Kronenberg L, Rimat G, Yates S, Studer B.

title: A global survey of type I secretion systems and the substrates in Gram-negative bacteria.
abstract: Type I secretion system (T1SS) is a special device employed by Gram-negative bacteria, which only contains three components but can mediate the transport of proteins through two cell membranes. Despite their important functions, the true distribution and diversity of T1SSs in Gram-negative bacteria remain unclear. Here, we started from annotating and clustering 50 sets of T1SSs with experimentally validated functions, followed by comprehensive screening of T1SSs from the genomes of 2996 representative bacterial strains with a homology-based detection strategy combined with gene organization analysis. In total, we found 4967 highly confident sets of T1SSs from 2037 strains, encompassing 13 phyla, 357 genera and 901 species. The T1SSs were divided into nine clusters, while Salmonella contains most of the clusters, among which many are specific to the genus. To more comprehensively and precisely identify T1SS substrate proteins (T1SPs), the evolutionary features of validated T1SPs were observed and used to expand the size of high-confidence T1SPs. We also trained multiple traditional machine-learning models, ensemblers, and protein language models to predict T1SPs. Comparisons by a cross-validation strategy and an independent testing dataset both demonstrated the superior performance of a Mamba-based model (T1SEstacker 3.0) over other machine-learning or language models, ensemblers and other state-of-the-art tools. We further applied the model to screen the T1SPs and observed their distribution across the representative bacterial genomes. In summary, the study made a systematic survey on T1SSs and their substrate proteins, providing important resources for the community studying bacterial T1SSs and other protein secretion systems, secreted proteins and virulence.
authors: Li J, Chen Z, Liu K, Zhang J, Kong W, Wang Y, Yu M, Wu J, Chen J, Hu X, Cao X, Liu X, Wang Y.

title: The H5N1 avian influenza threat: a European Perspective on Research Gaps and State of Preparedness.
abstract: H5N1 influenza clade 2.3.4.4b has spread from South East Asia through migratory birds since 2020. The expansion seeded frequent spillovers into wild and domestic mammals including cattle in the United States. While the risk for humans not in direct contact with infected animals is low, the widespread presence and opportunities for evolution constitutes a pandemic threat. If sustained human-to-human transmission (H2H) would emerge, there is limited time to mount a public health response. Initially, non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) are needed until vaccines are available. Experience with H5N1 viruses since 1997 suggests that infections are seen mostly in people born after 1968, indicating that people under sixty may be at particular risk. Closely monitoring viral diversity and evolution in wild life, and at the human animal interface, using integrated One Health surveillance and genome-based selection of viruses for further characterization for instance receptor affinity of H5N1 to human receptors is mandatory.

title: Inflammatory and transcriptional profiles associated with structural and functional recovery in pre-XDR/XDR tuberculosis.
abstract: BackgroundIn drug-resistant TB, bacteriology-based monitoring often fails to capture recovery. We aimed to identify baseline host inflammatory and transcriptional features associated with multidomain treatment recovery in pre-XDR/XDR-TB.MethodsWe conducted an ancillary analysis of a pilot clinical trial in patients with pre-XDR/XDR-TB (NCT02781909). Participants were assessed at baseline and during treatment using clinical, radiological, microbiological, and health-related quality-of-life measures, plasma biomarkers, and whole-blood transcriptomic profiling, analyzed in relation to treatment outcomes.ResultsMicrobiological and symptomatic improvement occurred earlier than radiological and functional recovery. Baseline elevated NLR, SII, and IL-6, and an increased expression of interferon-related genes as CD274 and GBP5, were associated with poorer radiological and HRQoL outcomes. IL-8 consistently correlated with symptom severity, radiological and functional outcomes. Previously published blood transcriptomic signatures were more strongly associated with radiological and HRQoL recovery than with early bacterial clearance.ConclusionsBacteriological cure precedes but does not ensure structural and functional recovery in pre-XDR/XDR-TB. Baseline inflammation identifies patients at risk of incomplete recovery, and IL-8 emerges as a candidate cross-domain monitoring biomarker. These findings support multidimensional treatment monitoring and a biological rationale for host-directed interventions targeting persistent inflammation.

authors: García-Illarramendi JM, Sopegno C, Fonseca KL, Arias L, Barbakadze K, Jikia I, Tsotskhalashvili M, Korinteli T, Avaliani Z, Tukvadze N, Vashakidze S, Farrés J, Vilaplana C.

title: Bifunctional cytochrome P450/ferredoxin is required for fungal phytochrome assembly at mitochondria.
abstract: Mitochondria act as dynamic signaling hubs intertwining cellular metabolism and environmental perception in fungi. Here, we elucidate the assembly of the red-light sensing phytochrome (FphA) at the mitochondrial outer membrane in Alternaria alternata. Phytochrome photoconversion strictly relies on biliverdin biosynthesis by heme oxygenases. While mammalian and plant heme oxygenases localize to the endoplasmic reticulum or chloroplasts, the fungal system uniquely repurposes the outer mitochondrial membrane. We demonstrate that the fungal heme oxygenases HoxA and HoxB form a heteromeric complex integrated into the membrane via mitochondrial import machinery components Mim1 and Mim2. At the mitochondrial surface, only HoxA binds directly to FphA. Genomic screening identified Bifunctional Cytochrome P450 Reductase/Ferredoxin A (BcfA) as the essential physiological electron donor. Quantitative kinetics established that BcfA operates as an asymmetric hub, displaying higher affinity for HoxB than HoxA. HoxB functions as a high-affinity kinetic tether locking the donor at the membrane boundary. Consequently, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of bcfA disrupts red-light signalling. Thus, a multi-protein mitochondrial complex evolved in fungi to wire light perception through spatial compartmentalization.
authors: Schuhmacher L, Landmark A, Jähring T, Müller A, Streng C, Fischer R.

title: In Vitro Activity of Cefiderocol against Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii and the Cefiderocol Resistance Mechanisms.
abstract: BackgroundExtensively drug-resistant and pandrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, pose a major threat due to limited treatment options and high mortality. Rising prevalence of carbapenem resistance has further complicated therapy, necessitating novel antimicrobial agents. Cefiderocol, a siderophore-conjugated cephalosporin, offers a promising therapeutic option against these multidrug-resistant pathogens.ObjectivesTo assess the in vitro activity of cefiderocol and key comparators against carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria from a Malaysian hospital.MethodsA total of 448 non-duplicate carbapenem-resistant bacterial strains collected from the University Malaya Medical Centre diagnostic laboratory from year 2018-2021 were included. Broth microdilution was used for susceptibility testing of cefiderocol and other agents relevant to the respective carbapenem-resistant organisms (CROs), in accordance with CLSI guidelines. Susceptibility was interpreted using CLSI breakpoints, with FDA breakpoints applied for tigecycline. Genotypic detection of antimicrobial resistance-associated genes was performed via polymerase chain reaction. Whole genome sequencing was performed on cefiderocol-resistant isolates for genetic characterisation.ResultsCefiderocol demonstrated the highest susceptibility rate for the tested CROs when compared to other antimicrobial agents. More than 90% of the carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates were susceptible to cefiderocol, whereas 81.2% of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates were susceptible. Among a total of 22 cefiderocol-resistant isolates, 17 isolates produced NDM-1 and 11 isolates produced PER or VEB ESBL.ConclusionsCefiderocol remains an effective treatment option for patients infected with CROs. Ongoing surveillance and antibiotic stewardship are essential to monitor the emergence of resistance and preserve the effectiveness of cefiderocol against multidrug-resistant pathogens.
authors: Wong JH, Woon JJ, Ponnampalavanar SSS, Yamashiro H, Miyagawa D, Onishi M, Takemura M, Yamano Y, Teh CSJ.

title: Developmental PFAS exposure impairs host resistance and is associated with immune-developmental molecular signatures in marine medaka.
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants with recognized immunotoxic potential, yet their effects on the developing immune system remain incompletely understood. Building directly on a previously established analytical and exposure framework for developmental PFAS exposure in this species, this study examined the immunotoxicity of legacy (PFOS, PFOA) and replacement (PFHxS, PFHxA, PFBS, GenX) PFAS in marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma) during a later developmental window relevant to T-cell maturation (12-19 days post-hatch). At the organismal level, larvae were assessed for immune competence using a host resistance assay following bacterial challenge. To explore candidate molecular processes associated with these organismal responses, we additionally profiled whole-body metabolomes and transcriptomes and integrated the two through joint pathway analysis. Developmental exposure to GenX, PFBS, and PFOA significantly reduced post-challenge survival relative to challenged controls (50% survival), with survival falling to 7% (GenX), 13% (PFBS), and 0% (PFOA, 5 ng/mL), with effects that were compound-specific rather than monotonically dose-dependent, demonstrating that several replacement PFAS impair host resistance at environmentally relevant concentrations. Metabolomic and transcriptomic profiling identified candidate molecular processes associated with these exposures, with over-representation analysis of nominally responsive genes recovering, among a broader set of enriched terms, terms related to immune and hematopoietic development-including T-cell activation, T-cell differentiation, and thymus development-across multiple PFAS. Joint pathway analysis highlighted central energy metabolism, particularly the citrate (TCA) cycle, as a recurring feature across compounds. Together, these findings establish that replacement PFAS can functionally compromise host resistance during early development and provide molecular hypotheses implicating immune-developmental and metabolic processes worthy of targeted follow-up.
authors: DiBona ER, Lu Y, Elliott J, Labeille RO, Abdulla H, Seemann F.

title: Trace metal contamination, microbiological quality, and human health risk assessment of edible oyster (Crassostrea belcheri) from the Cox's Bazar Coast, Bangladesh.
abstract: Oysters are effective bioindicators of aquatic contamination. Their filter-feeding behavior causes them to bioaccumulate heavy metals and emerging contaminants from coastal waters. This poses both ecological and human health risks through seafood consumption. This study evaluated trace metal contamination, microbiological quality, and human health risk in Crassostrea belcheri from the Cox's Bazar coast, Bangladesh. Twelve trace metals were quantified in the soft tissue. Na, K, and Ca dominated the metal profile, followed by Zn, Mg, Fe, Cu, Mn, Ni, Cr, Pb, and Cd, which occurred at comparatively low levels. Most metals exceeded Bangladesh's national shellfish contamination guideline, except Cd. This points to a broader baseline contamination burden, even where dietary-intake indices suggested low risk. Estimated Daily Intake values for all metals stayed within permissible limits. This corresponds to negligible non-carcinogenic hazard. However, carcinogenic risk estimates for Cd, Cr, and Ni exceeded acceptable thresholds. This indicates a real long-term cancer risk from chronic consumption, despite the reassuring non-carcinogenic profile. Escherichia coli was detected in microbiological screening of collected oysters, whereas Vibrio cholerae and Salmonella spp. were not detected in any of the analyzed samples. This suggests a relatively low burden among the tested pathogens, though other microbial hazards cannot be ruled out. Trace metal contamination in C. belcheri poses a greater long-term health concern than national guidelines or acute intake thresholds alone would suggest. Regular monitoring is recommended to protect consumer health and support quality assurance for export markets that depend on this regionally important but understudied resource.
authors: Nasrin K, Bhattacharjee SC, Anisuzzaman M, Hasan M, Islam MA, Islam MI, Islam MT, Hasan MR, Ahmed S, Islam MSMM.

title: Evolution-guided association mapping using long-read genomes from a self-identified Black or African American cohort in  All of Us
abstract: Background:  : Identifying functional variants that influence human health remains a challenge in human genetics. Conventional genotype-phenotype association studies test millions of variants, imposing a substantial multiple-testing burden as genomic and biobank datasets expand in size and variant diversity. Additionally, the contribution of structural variation, which is a substantial driver of genetic diversity, remains underexplored in these studies. Signatures of recent positive selection offer a powerful biological basis for prioritizing potentially functional variation, although demographic history can confound their detection and interpretation in these analyses.  Results:  : We performed evolution-guided association mapping using long-read genomes from 1,027 self-identified Black or African American participants in the All of Us Research Program and short-read genomes from an additional 38,552 matched participants of African-ancestry. Using demography-calibrated inferences, we identified 228 genomic regions with local ancestry enrichment or depletion and 1,616 candidate loci showing putative recent positive selection signals. These loci were enriched for genic and regulatory sequences, as well as previously reported eQTL, sQTL, and GWAS associations. Leveraging the resolution of the long-read data, we mapped 15 structural variants to these candidate loci, including 10 located within 1,000 base pairs of putative cis-regulatory enhancers. Admixture- and selection-based phenome-wide association testing identified 13 and 446 nominal associations, respectively, 17 of which remained significant following replication and meta-analysis.  Conclusions:  : Our results support the use of evolutionary signatures as a robust framework for uncovering clinically relevant variation, including structural variants, in underrepresented populations.
authors: Soisangwan N, Garimella KV, Schatz MC, Eichler EE, Sedlazeck FJ, Talkowski ME, Cunial F, Lee SK, All of Us Research Program Long Read Working Group, Hsieh P.

title: Pervasive chromothripsis drives pleural mesothelioma to impact gene function and patient survival
abstract: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a tumour type showing high structural complexity but the full spectrum of variants present and their impacts are poorly understood. We comprehensively describe the mutational landscape of mesothelioma, exploiting a large (N=443) cohort profiling the tumour genome and transcriptome in parallel. We find that the majority of candidate driver variants are mediated by copy number alterations (CNAs) and discover high frequencies of complex rearrangements across most tumours, dominated by chromothripsis (74% of tumours) and chromoplexy (59%). Chromothripsis contributes to significant CNA hotspots to delete known PM tumour suppressor genes such as  CDKN2A, NF2 and  BAP1 , thought to be among the earliest events in PM development; and the presence of chromothripsis is associated with significantly worse patient survival. We also discover multi-faceted crosstalk between the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes during PM evolution, involving alterations to both genomes, and mitochondrial expression changes associated with subtypes and chromothripsis.
authors: Sherwood K, Aitken S, Silk R, Halachev M, Fox S, Bendixsen D, Hamdan A, Blyth KG, Semple CA.

title: Temporal organization of the Plasmodium falciparum transcriptome prioritises genetic polymorphisms associated with artemisinin response
abstract: Abstract  Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) have substantially reduced the global burden of malaria, but the emergence and spread of artemisinin partial resistance (ART-R) threatens these gains. Although mutations in Plasmodium falciparum kelch13 (pfk13) are established mediators of ART-R, they do not fully explain variation in parasite responses, highlighting the need for complementary markers. We integrated six independent intra-erythrocytic developmental cycle (IDC) transcriptomic datasets by harmonic regression and random-effects meta-analysis, followed by network analyses, protein structural modelling, population genomics and ex vivo dihydroartemisinin susceptibility data, to identify candidate P. falciparum polymorphisms associated with artemisinin response. The meta-analysis identified 2,842 of 5,292 genes as significantly rhythmic across the 48-hour IDC, including those encoding PfK13 and PfMDR1. Integration with whole-genome sequences of Ugandan field isolates prioritized 13 nonsynonymous variants across 10 genes, encoding PfAP2-G, PfPX1, PfACS7, PfACS1a, PfRESA3, PfDRPC and PfA8IJP together with three proteins of unknown function, all transcriptionally co-timed with pfk13. Polymorphisms in pfpx1 have independently been implicated in artemisinin susceptibility, consistent with our prioritization. These candidates are potential complementary mediators of artemisinin response. Beyond them, the pipeline itself is transferable to other resistance phenotypes and periodic transcriptional programmes.

title: Nutrient and Organic Matter Driven Reorganization of Phytoplankton Communities Downstream of Wastewater Discharge in the Styr River (Ukraine)
abstract: Abstract  The study investigated changes in the phytoplankton community of the Styr River in the area affected by wastewater discharge from a nuclear power plant. The aim was to assess the effects of nutrient loading associated with wastewater discharge on phytoplankton species composition, abundance, biomass, and community structure. Samples were collected in May - August 2024 at two river sites located upstream and downstream of the wastewater discharge point. Water samples were analyzed for dissolved organic carbon (DOC), total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP). UV–Vis optical indices indicated a downstream shift toward more aromatic and higher-molecular-weight DOM characteristics, consistent with changes in the composition of the dissolved organic matter pool. Phytoplankton was assessed in terms of abundance, biomass, mean cell biomass, and taxonomic structure. Correlation analysis and principal component analysis (PCA) were used to examine relationships between hydrochemical and biological variables. Downstream of the discharge point, DOC, TN, and TP concentrations increased by 19.4%, 56.5%, and 72.7%, respectively, compared with the reference site. Against this background, phytoplankton abundance decreased from 3.0 × 10⁶ to 0.5 × 10⁶ cells dm⁻³, while biomass decreased from 0.70 to 0.15 mg dm⁻³. At the same time, mean cell biomass increased, indicating a shift in the size structure of the community. Bacillariophyta dominated upstream, accounting for 79% of total abundance and 85% of total biomass. Downstream, Chlorophyta and Euglenophyta became predominant, whereas the contribution of diatoms declined markedly. The saprobity index increased from 1.96 to 2.61, indicating increased organic loading. Correlation analysis showed negative relationships between nutrient concentrations and Bacillariophyta, but positive relationships with Chlorophyta and Euglenophyta. PCA confirmed clear spatial separation of the phytoplankton communities along the trophic gradient. Overall, increased organic matter and nutrient concentrations in the discharge-affected area were accompanied by a restructuring of the phytoplankton community, characterized by a reduced contribution of diatoms and an increased contribution of taxa tolerant of organic pollution.
authors: Biedunkova O, Kuznietsov P, Pryshchepa A, Statnyk I.

title: Self-organized colloidal growth of stromatolites
abstract: Abstract  Stromatolites have been widely regarded as key biosignatures of early life, yet the controls on their morphogenesis and diversity remain poorly constrained. Here, we investigate Mesoproterozoic ironstones from North China featuring stromatolitic structures and composed of laminated Fe(III)-oxyhydroxide colloids. Microstructural observations and colloidal stability calculations indicate that terrestrial colloids flocculated rapidly upon mixing with seawater in an estuarine environment and aggregated on the seafloor. We then numerically simulate the forming processes of stromatolites via diffusion-limited aggregation and surface diffusion (DLA–SD) mechanism and reveal that stromatolitic morphogenesis is primarily controlled by depositional and aggregation dynamics of colloids, which are related to geochemical and hydrodynamic conditions in estuaries. This DLA–SD framework also provides quantitative insights into the microbial sediment-trapping mechanisms for the formation of carbonate stromatolites and reveals that the diversification of morphologies of stromatolite were linked to the evolution of oceanic chemistry and microbial communities throughout the Earth history.
authors: Zhou M, Qiu W, Ballhaus C.

title: Genome-Wide Association Mapping Identifies QTLs for Yield Components under Heat Stress and Cold Tolerance during Seedling Establishment in Mung Bean (Vigna radiata)
abstract: Abstract    Background.  Heat stress during reproductive development and cold stress during seedling establishment are major constraints on mung bean (  Vigna radiata  L. Wilczek) production. However, the quantitative trait loci (QTLs) underlying yield stability under heat stress and cold tolerance during seedling establishment remain largely unknown. A diversity panel comprising 126 mung bean accessions was evaluated for responses to heat and cold stress. Heat-stress responses were quantified as reductions in pod length and seed number per pod relative to control conditions. Cold tolerance during seedling establishment was assessed using germination rate, seedling vigor, and a visual chilling-injury score. Genome-wide association mapping was performed using the multi-locus FarmCPU model, stress-response phenotypes, and 710,906 high-quality single-nucleotide polymorphisms anchored to the JL7 reference genome. Allelic-effect analyses were subsequently conducted for each lead locus to distinguish robust QTLs associated with common alleles from potentially unreliable rare-allele associations. Results.  QTLs associated with heat-stress responses and cold tolerance were located in distinct genomic regions. A major QTL controlling pod-length reduction under heat stress was identified on chromosome 3 and was consistently detected under two independent heat-stress regimes. This stable heat-tolerance QTL was associated with a common allele that had a large phenotypic effect. Two stable QTLs associated with common alleles were identified for cold tolerance during seedling establishment: one for seedling vigor under cold stress on chromosome 7 at 2.69 Mb and another for chilling-injury score on chromosome 6 at 19.87 Mb. These QTL regions contained biologically plausible candidate genes, including a gene encoding an FKBP62-type immunophilin co-chaperone within the chromosome 3 heat-tolerance QTL and genes encoding the CBF/DREB1 regulator CAMTA5 and a DnaJ/Hsp40 co-chaperone within the chromosome 7 cold-tolerance QTL. Conclusions.  Genome-wide association mapping combined with allelic-effect validation identified stable QTLs associated with yield components under heat stress and cold tolerance during seedling establishment in mung bean. The heat- and cold-tolerance QTLs were genomically independent, indicating that pyramiding distinct loci will be necessary to combine tolerance to both stresses. These QTLs, particularly those associated with common alleles, represent promising targets for marker-assisted breeding of climate-resilient mung bean cultivars.
authors: Aesomnuek O, Aesomnuk W, Thunnom B, Poncheewin W, Ruanjaichon V, Laosatit K, Somta P, Arikit S, Wanchana S.

title: Quantitative Systems Biology of Interplay Among Three Transcription Factors NRF2, sMAF, and BACH1 Modulating Cellular Antioxidant Response
abstract: Background:  The antioxidant response element (ARE) is regulated by three competing transcription factors (TF) that bind as dimeric complexes. The NRF2–MAFG heterodimer activates transcription; the MAFG homodimer, which has no transactivation domain, and the BACH1–MAFG heterodimer silence it. All three TFs compete for the ARE, so the transcriptional output is set by a three-way competition rather than by NRF2 abundance alone. All these TFs are promising therapeutic targets in various diseases, with candidate compounds currently under development. However, successful drug design requires a detailed understanding of their complex interplay at ARE activation. Quantitative systems biology (QSB) modelling of these triple competitive systems provides a means to disentangle these dynamics in different diseases. In this paper, we developed a QSB model of NRF2-sMAF-BACH1-ARE system as a submodule of a larger upstream network that control cellular oxidative stress in various pathologies and aging. Methods. We built a quantitative systems biology model of the three-way competition at the ARE: NRF2, small MAF (sMAFG) and BACH1 interconvert with three dimers (the NRF2-MAFG activator, the MAFG homodimer and the BACH1-MAFG repressor) that compete for one pool of ARE sites; heme sequesters free BACH1 (12 species, 7 reactions; SBML L3V2). Binding constants came from published SPR and EMSA data; four remaining quantities were fitted to a nine-point luciferase titration. Genome-wide classification of antioxidant gene promoters by ARE affinity was carried out, and affinity scale was transferred to a position weight matrix that was applied to the promoters of 172 antioxidant and NRF2-target genes against 394 controls. Results. The dependence of activation and repression of the ARE on NRF2 and sMAF levels was calculated and calibrated against experimental data. Output is set by the shared sMAF pool: activation rises monotonically in NRF2 but peaks in small MAF at 0.173 µM. NRF2 acts as the switch variable and small MAF as a two-sided gain setting. BACH1 inhibits competitively, sliding the dose-response along the NRF2 axis without lowering the saturation level: 0.3 µM holds 54% of the sites and halves activation when BACH1–sMAF dimerisation is tight, and is inert at 10 µM. Heme relieves repression near 0.14 µM by returning sMAF to the activator. Using experimental dissociation constants for various SNP in the ARE, the model results demonstrated that sequence identity alters occupancy three-fold without changing response shape, and sorts real promoters: the high-affinity class is enriched 3.05-fold among antioxidant genes (odds ratio 3.39, p = 1.9∙ 10⁻⁴), recovers the curated NRF2 programme, and is predicted to be 6.5% occupied at resting NRF2 against 1.2% for the low-affinity class. We discussed the obtained results in the context of the potential pharmacological role of NRF2-sMAF-BACH1-ARE system as a therapeutic target for current drug design in various diseases and aging. Conclusions. The ARE step is graded, reading out an upstream sensor rather than creating a switch. Its sensitivity lies not in the well-measured DNA-binding layer but in the dimerisation layer, which is fitted or assumed and decides whether repression occurs at all; measuring the NRF2–sMAF and BACH1–sMAF affinities would provide the strongest constraint on the system.
authors: Goltsov A, Kel A, Goryanin I.

title: Photoelectrochemical biosensor using CoPP to quench PTCA for the detection of mip gene fragment.
abstract: Legionella pneumophila is a harmful Gram-negative aquatic pathogen that causes Legionnaires' disease, and sensitive detection of this bacterium is essential for epidemiological investigation. Herein, a photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensor based on 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic acid (PTCA) as the photoactive material and tetraphenylporphyrin cobalt (CoPP) as the signal quencher was constructed for the detection of the macrophage infectivity potentiator (mip) gene fragment from Legionella pneumophila. PTCA with favorable optoelectronic properties and film-forming capacity provided a strong initial photocurrent response. Gold nanoparticles (Au NPs) were electrodeposited on the electrode surface to immobilize DNA S1 through Au-S interactions. After target-induced DNA hybridization, CoPP was intercalated into the formed DNA duplex, which efficiently quenched the PEC signal of PTCA. Benefiting from the signal quenching effect of CoPP towards PTCA, the proposed biosensor achieved quantitative detection of the mip gene fragment in the range from 100 fmol/L to 1 µmol/L with a detection limit of 33.3 fmol/L. This work provides an analytical tool and shows promise for practical screening of the mip gene fragment of Legionella pneumophila in respiratory specimens with high bacterial loads.
journal: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
authors: Zhang F, Lu L, Li S, Gong L, Li M.

title: Synthesizing multi-omics evidence of interface-specific selection in lung adenocarcinoma metastasis: A trait-origin-interface-function framework across lymph-node and brain ecosystems.
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) mortality is driven largely by metastatic progression, yet lymph-node metastasis (LNM) and parenchymal brain metastasis (BrM) arise in fundamentally different immune and anatomical ecosystems. Here, we present an integrative review that conceptually synthesizes published genomic, single-cell, spatial-transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic findings. Our trait-origin-interface-function (TOIF) framework maps individual claims to trait origin, anatomical interface, metastatic stage and functional output, with separate annotations for evidence type and study context. In LNM, lymphatic access and nodal occupation are associated with remodeling of antigen presentation, progenitor T-cell maintenance, lymphoid organization, and immune-cell export; however, evidence for individual tumor-immune communication axes remains uneven. In BrM, neurovascular entry, perivascular survival, glial-myeloid signaling, metabolic adaptation, and restricted effector access represent separable bottlenecks. Cross-platform evidence indicates that shared genomic ancestry can coexist with site-enriched transcriptional, immune, and metabolic states, while temporal and lineage-resolved measurements help distinguish their possible pre-existence, selective expansion and acquisition after tissue exposure. We therefore propose a TOIF framework that links each candidate mechanism to the omics layers that support it, the spatial context in which it operates, and the experiment needed to test causality. This framework clarifies why similar low-cytotoxicity phenotypes may reflect distinct mechanisms in nodal and brain lesions, and provides a basis for multi-omics biomarker development and stage-matched therapeutic investigation in LUAD metastasis.
authors: Xu Y, Zhang R, Hu Y, Yang M, Shan H, Liang T, Guo L.
